title: Tricyclic Antidepressants as Prospective alpha-Synucleinopathy Fighters: Evidence of Protein Binding and Antiaggregation Activity.
authors: Khairutdinov, Bulat I; Khaibrakhmanova, Diliara R; Leisi, Evgeniia V; Sidorova, Ekaterina R; Sofronov, Yegor A; Muronetz, Vladimir I; Zuev, Yuriy F; Sedov, Igor A
one_liner_zh: 该文用分子动力学模拟结合NMR研究三环抗抑郁药与无序蛋白α-synuclein的非特异性多位点结合及抗聚集机制，对象为IDP且涉及结合机制建模，但互作对象是小分子而非蛋白-蛋白互作，故评7分。
abstract: Intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) like alpha-synuclein are pivotal in neurodegenerative diseases but present formidable challenges for drug discovery due to their conformational heterogeneity and lack of defined binding pockets. Here, we report the finding that clinically approved tricyclic antidepressants imipramine, amitriptyline, and doxepin bind directly to monomeric alpha-synuclein and inhibit its fibrillation, a key process in Parkinson's pathology. Using a combination of NMR spectroscopy (WaterLOGSY and chemical shift perturbation, CSP) and molecular dynamics simulation methods, we elucidate a nonspecific, multiligand binding mechanism of tricyclic antidepressants predominantly targeting the C-terminal domain of the protein. The experimental CSP magnitudes correlate with the inhibitory potency of ligands, with imipramine emerging as the most potent inhibitor, and agree with the contact probabilities with different residues from simulations. The protein-ligand binding is driven by a dynamic combination of electrostatic attraction of positively charged ligands to anionic side chains, pi-stacking with aromatic residues, and hydrophobic contacts. Moreover, simulations show that a single ligand molecule frequently engages in simultaneous salt-bridge and pi-stacking interactions, unlike some previously studied alpha-synuclein binders. Our findings position tricyclic antidepressants as promising scaffolds for targeting alpha-synuclein and demonstrate the efficiency of molecular dynamics approaches for the description of interactions between small drug molecules and IDPs.
abstract_zh: 像α-突触核蛋白（alpha-synuclein）这样的固有无序蛋白（IDPs）在神经退行性疾病中至关重要，但由于其构象异质性和缺乏明确的结合口袋，给药物发现带来了巨大挑战。在此，我们报告了一项发现：临床批准的三环类抗抑郁药丙咪嗪（imipramine）、阿米替林（amitriptyline）和多塞平（doxepin）直接结合单体α-突触核蛋白并抑制其纤维化，这是帕金森病病理中的一个关键过程。通过结合核磁共振波谱（WaterLOGSY和化学位移扰动，CSP）以及分子动力学模拟方法，我们阐明了一种非特异性的多配体结合机制，三环类抗抑郁药主要靶向蛋白质的C端结构域。实验CSP幅度与配体的抑制效力相关，其中丙咪嗪成为最有效的抑制剂，并且与模拟中不同残基的接触概率一致。蛋白质-配体结合由带正电配体与阴离子侧链的静电吸引、与芳香族残基的π-堆积以及疏水接触的动态组合驱动。此外，模拟显示，单个配体分子经常同时参与盐桥和π-堆积相互作用，这与先前研究的一些α-突触核蛋白结合剂不同。我们的发现将三环类抗抑郁药定位为靶向α-突触核蛋白的有前景的支架，并展示了分子动力学方法在描述小药物分子与IDPs之间相互作用方面的效率。
